r01: Is the delivered image itself clearly a screenshot or user interface, a flat poster, advertisement, page, document, infographic, diagram, illustration, painting reproduction, or an obvious computer-rendered scene? Answer YES for such excluded content even if attractive or legible. Answer NO for a photograph of a physical scene or object with meaningful surrounding context, including labels, signs, packages, screens, artworks or sculpture. If genuinely uncertain, answer NO.
r02: Check the entire frame before rating. Does it primarily reproduce a flat graphic work or digital interface: poster, magazine cover, printed page, chart, artwork, drawing, screenshot or obvious 3D render? A near-full-frame copy is excluded even if photographed. A photograph of a physical object or scene with visible depth, perspective or meaningful surroundings stays eligible, even when text or art appears in it. Answer YES only when the exclusion is clear; otherwise NO.
r03: Answer YES if the image is a flat poster, advertisement, page, chart, drawing or painting presented as the content; a screenshot with app/browser/game controls; or an obvious computer-generated render. A beautifully designed graphic is still excluded. Answer NO for an actual photographed scene, packaging, signage, physical display or sculpture with context and for uncertain cases. This is a domain decision, not a technical or aesthetic rating.
r04: Is the visible frame clearly outside the photographic domain? YES: a near-full-frame reproduction of a poster, advertisement, document, diagram, illustration, painting, screenshot or obvious synthetic graphic. NO: a photographed bottle, product, sign, screen or artwork as a physical object in a scene, or any uncertain origin. Do not decide from blur, darkness, color, subject attractiveness or image quality. Inspect visible layout and physical context.
r05: Identify the medium of the whole image. Exclude a flat graphic design or reproduction, including posters with typography over a photograph, pages and charts; exclude interface screenshots and unmistakable computer renders. Do not exclude a normal photograph merely for containing printed text, a sign, a photograph of an object, art in a surrounding scene, or blur. Is the image clearly excluded under that rule? Answer YES if excluded and NO if eligible or uncertain.
